Valley Girl
VAL-ee gurl
noun (Gen X slang)
From the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles (Encino, Sherman Oaks, Tarzana), where affluent teenage girls of the late 1970s and early 1980s developed a recognizable speech — rising "uptalk" intonation, like as filler, totally, as if, gag me with a spoon, grody to the max. Frank Zappa and his fourteen-year-old daughter Moon Unit parodied it on the hit single "Valley Girl" (1982); the film Valley Girl (1983) and the Sherman Oaks Galleria shopping mall became its icons. The term later named the type: a stereotypically shallow, mall-centered, status-conscious young woman.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Valley Girl was a type before she was a joke: a daughter of plenty, raised among malls, credit cards, and the sunny assumption that nothing serious would ever be asked of her. Her dialect was the sound of a life without weight — every sentence lifting into a question, every opinion either "totally" or "gag me." Scripture is not cruel to such a girl, and neither should we be; but it is honest about the posture. Isaiah saw the daughters of Zion who "walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go" (Isa 3:16), and the Lord warned that the ornaments would be taken away. The apostle points a young woman to a different adornment: "not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; but (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works" (1Ti 2:9-10). "Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised" (Pro 31:30). And Titus 2 gives the cure that a mall cannot: older women who are "teachers of good things" (Tit 2:3), discipling younger women into substance. The Valley Girl does not need mockery; she needs a mother in the faith and a Savior who gives her life weight.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen X label (1982, Zappa’s "Valley Girl") for the affluent San Fernando Valley teen and her uptalk-and-like dialect; Scripture answers her shallowness not with mockery but with the adornment of good works and the fear of the LORD (Pro 31:30).

VALLEY GIRL, n. (Gen X slang, early 1980s, Los Angeles) A teenage girl from the affluent San Fernando Valley; by extension, any young woman of stereotypically shallow, mall-centered, status-conscious manner.

Valspeak — her dialect: uptalk, like, totally, as if, whatever, gag me with a spoon, grody to the max, fer sure.

Icons: the Zappa single (1982), the film Valley Girl (1983), the Sherman Oaks Galleria; later echoed by Clueless (1995).

Webster 1828: VALLEY, n. plural valleys. [Latin vallis. See Vale.] 1. A hollow or low tract of land between hills or mountains. 2. A low extended plain, usually alluvial, penetrated or washed by a river. …

Decode for parents: much of the dialect your daughter speaks today — uptalk and like — was born here; what she needs is not ridicule but substance.

Key Scripture

Isa 3:16 — "Moreover the LORD saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet:"

1Ti 2:9 — "In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;"

1Ti 2:10 — "But (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works."

Pro 31:30 — "Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised."

Tit 2:3 — "The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;"

Modern Corruption

The Valley Girl is a daughter of plenty taught that nothing weighty will ever be asked of her; Scripture adorns a young woman with good works and the fear of the LORD, and supplies older women to teach her.

expand to see more

A life without weight. The trouble with the Valley Girl was never the accent; it was the world that produced it — affluence without duty, a mall in place of a church, and a culture that expected nothing of its daughters but consumption and charm. Isaiah’s daughters of Zion (Isa 3:16) were the same type in an older costume, and the prophet’s point was that ornaments do not survive judgment. Raise a girl on surfaces and she will speak in surfaces.

The Titus 2 answer. Mockery is easy and useless. The Lord’s remedy is relational: aged women who are "teachers of good things" (Tit 2:3), a mother and grandmothers who show a girl that a woman who fears the LORD is praised (Pro 31:30) and that the best adornment is good works (1Ti 2:10). Many a Valley Girl grew into a godly mother once someone handed her something worth carrying.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

San Fernando Valley, Los Angeles (late 1970s) → Zappa’s "Valley Girl" (1982) → the film (1983) → Clueless (1995) → modern uptalk; Scripture’s answer: good works and Titus 2 discipleship.
